platformRules._comment: Sections 3 + 5: Generates Assessment Signals and deterministic scoring that leads to platform selection

scoringRules._comment: Section 3 – Each rule generates an Assessment Signal with Response Evidence, Interpretation, Why It Matters, and Platform Impact

Q001.concept: Existing ServiceNow or ITSM Capability Reuse
Q001.description: The assessment identifies existing ServiceNow or ITSM tooling as a reusable enterprise component.
Q001.whyItMatters: Reusing an existing ITSM platform reduces procurement risk, accelerates delivery, and avoids duplicate tooling across the enterprise.

Q001.concept: Existing Microsoft M365 or Power Platform Capability Reuse
Q001.description: The assessment identifies existing M365, SharePoint, Teams, or Power Platform components as reusable.
Q001.whyItMatters: Reusing licensed M365 components eliminates incremental procurement and aligns the solution with the existing BC Government platform investment.

Q001.concept: Existing Salesforce or CRM Capability Reuse
Q001.description: The assessment identifies existing Salesforce or CRM tooling as a reusable enterprise component.
Q001.whyItMatters: Reusing an existing CRM platform reduces onboarding cost, leverages established data models, and avoids parallel citizen-engagement systems.

Q001.description: The assessment indicates no existing enterprise capabilities can be reused, suggesting a greenfield build.
Q001.whyItMatters: Absence of reusable components increases delivery risk and cost — a strong business case is required before selecting a custom build path.

Q002.concept: Microsoft M365 Shared Service Standard Alignment
Q002.description: The assessment confirms the solution aligns to the BC Government M365 shared service standard.
Q002.whyItMatters: Alignment to M365 shared service standards supports Power Platform adoption under existing licensing, avoids procurement overhead, and reduces shadow IT risk.

Q002.concept: ServiceNow ITSM Shared Service Standard Alignment
Q002.description: The assessment confirms the solution aligns to the BC Government ServiceNow ITSM shared service standard.
Q002.whyItMatters: Alignment to the BC Government ITSM standard reduces evaluation overhead, supports existing enterprise licensing, and signals a well-understood operational model.

Q002.description: The assessment confirms the solution aligns to an established Salesforce or CRM shared service standard.
Q002.whyItMatters: Alignment to an existing CRM shared service standard supports platform reuse, reduces procurement complexity, and signals established governance patterns.

Q002.concept: Non-Standard or No Shared Service Alignment
Q002.description: The assessment indicates the solution does not align to current enterprise shared service standards.
Q002.whyItMatters: Absence of shared service alignment increases governance risk and may require ARB exception approval — a detailed justification is recommended.

Q009.description: The assessment identifies dedicated ITSM roles such as incident managers and change approvers.
Q009.whyItMatters: Role-based ITSM functions require a platform with built-in role hierarchies, workflow governance, and structured access controls.

Q009.description: The assessment requires enterprise SSO and privileged role access controls.
Q009.whyItMatters: Enterprise IAM requirements favour platforms with native SSO, MFA, and RBAC integration to reduce identity risk.

Q010.description: The assessment requires comprehensive audit logging of system and user actions.
Q010.whyItMatters: Audit trail completeness is a compliance requirement and a key platform differentiator for regulated government environments.

Q010.description: The assessment requires structured incident and change approval workflows.
Q010.whyItMatters: Change management and approval routing are core ITSM capabilities that favour purpose-built enterprise service management platforms.

Q010.description: The assessment requires integration with SIEM or security event management tools.
Q010.whyItMatters: SIEM integration favours platforms with mature security tooling, API-based event ingestion, and alert-to-incident automation.

CLOUD_SAAS_001.description: The assessment requires comprehensive IT service management capabilities.
CLOUD_SAAS_001.whyItMatters: Enterprise ITSM platforms provide mature incident, request, problem, change and SLA management capabilities that are not replicated by CRM or low-code platforms.

CLOUD_SAAS_001.description: The assessment requires a service desk with incident and service request management.
CLOUD_SAAS_001.whyItMatters: Service desk and incident management are primary ITSM platform drivers, strongly favouring purpose-built solutions over general workflow tools.

CLOUD_SAAS_001.description: The assessment requires customer relationship management capabilities.
CLOUD_SAAS_001.whyItMatters: CRM requirements strongly favour purpose-built CRM platforms. Deploying an ITSM platform for CRM needs creates unnecessary complexity and cost.

CLOUD_SAAS_001.description: The assessment requires a public-facing or citizen portal.
CLOUD_SAAS_001.whyItMatters: Citizen-facing services require platforms with strong portal capabilities, accessibility support, and scalable public-access licensing.

CLOUD_SAAS_001.description: The assessment requires low-code or citizen developer capabilities.
CLOUD_SAAS_001.whyItMatters: Low-code requirements favour platforms designed for business team delivery with minimal developer dependency, available under existing BC Government licensing.

CLOUD_SAAS_002.description: The assessment requires workflow automation and approval routing capabilities.
CLOUD_SAAS_002.whyItMatters: Workflow and approval routing depth is a key differentiator between enterprise platforms and lightweight tools such as simple form builders.

CLOUD_SAAS_002.description: The assessment indicates significant gaps between requirements and out-of-the-box platform capabilities.
CLOUD_SAAS_002.whyItMatters: Significant customization requirements may favour a custom build or a highly extensible enterprise platform over a constrained SaaS product.

CLOUD_SAAS_002.description: The assessment indicates requirements are largely met out of the box by a commercial platform.
CLOUD_SAAS_002.whyItMatters: Strong out-of-the-box fit reduces implementation risk, lowers cost, and favours established SaaS platforms over custom development.

CLOUD_CONSTRAINT_001.description: The assessment indicates no blocking cloud deployment constraints.
CLOUD_CONSTRAINT_001.whyItMatters: Absence of cloud deployment blockers supports the viability of SaaS-hosted enterprise platforms and reduces procurement risk.

CLOUD_CONSTRAINT_001.description: The assessment identifies data residency or Canadian data sovereignty requirements.
CLOUD_CONSTRAINT_001.whyItMatters: Data residency requirements favour platforms with confirmed Canadian or BC Government-approved data centre options to satisfy privacy obligations.

CLOUD_BUILD_001.description: The assessment indicates custom build is not justified or recommended for this use case.
CLOUD_BUILD_001.whyItMatters: Evidence against custom build strongly supports SaaS platform selection, reduces delivery risk, and is consistent with BC Government digital procurement guidelines.

CLOUD_BUILD_001.description: The assessment identifies requirements that cannot be met by any existing commercial platform.
CLOUD_BUILD_001.whyItMatters: Unique mandate requirements that cannot be satisfied by COTS platforms may justify a custom build investment, subject to a full business case.

CLOUD_BUILD_001.description: The assessment values enterprise platform maturity and proven delivery track records.
CLOUD_BUILD_001.whyItMatters: Platform maturity and proven track record reduce delivery risk, support ARB governance approval, and signal long-term vendor sustainability.

CLOUD_BUILD_002.description: The assessment indicates SaaS platforms are more cost-effective than custom development over the solution lifecycle.
CLOUD_BUILD_002.whyItMatters: TCO analysis favouring SaaS reduces the justification for custom build and supports platform procurement through existing enterprise agreements.

CLOUD_BUILD_002.description: The assessment indicates custom development is the more cost-effective long-term option.
CLOUD_BUILD_002.whyItMatters: Where custom build is cost-justified, the business case must fully account for maintenance, security patching, and long-term capability requirements.

CLOUD_BUILD_002.description: The assessment considers implementation and total cost of ownership in platform selection.
CLOUD_BUILD_002.whyItMatters: Implementation cost analysis is a key factor in BC Government platform procurement decisions and ARB business case requirements.

PLAT_CRM_001.description: The assessment identifies ITSM capabilities as the primary requirement, distinguishing it from CRM needs.
PLAT_CRM_001.whyItMatters: ITSM-focused requirements indicate a ServiceNow-class platform rather than a CRM platform — conflating ITSM with CRM leads to poor platform fit.

PLAT_CRM_001.description: The assessment explicitly excludes CRM as a requirement.
PLAT_CRM_001.whyItMatters: Explicit CRM exclusion signals that a CRM-centric platform such as Salesforce is not the right architectural fit for this use case.

PLAT_CRM_001.description: The assessment requires customer relationship management or citizen-facing portal capabilities.
PLAT_CRM_001.whyItMatters: CRM and citizen portal requirements are a primary driver for Salesforce platform selection in BC Government service delivery contexts.

PLAT_CRM_001.description: The assessment requires case management capabilities for citizen service delivery.
PLAT_CRM_001.whyItMatters: Case management for citizen services is a key Salesforce Government Cloud use case with established BC Government precedent.

PLAT_CRM_002.description: The assessment identifies this as an internal or staff-facing solution rather than a citizen-facing service.
PLAT_CRM_002.whyItMatters: Internal staff-facing solutions favour ITSM or Power Platform over citizen-oriented CRM platforms, reducing unnecessary licensing cost.

PLAT_CRM_002.description: The assessment requires an externally accessible citizen portal.
PLAT_CRM_002.whyItMatters: External citizen-facing portals require platforms designed for public-scale access, accessibility compliance, and session management.

PLAT_CRM_002.description: The assessment requires a staff-facing knowledge base or self-service portal.
PLAT_CRM_002.whyItMatters: Staff self-service and knowledge management capabilities are a core strength of enterprise ITSM platforms, reducing frontline service desk demand.

PLAT_WORKFLOW_001.description: The assessment requires complex incident routing with multi-step triage and escalation logic.
PLAT_WORKFLOW_001.whyItMatters: Complex incident routing and escalation requires a mature ITSM workflow engine — this cannot be adequately served by lightweight workflow tools.

PLAT_WORKFLOW_001.description: The assessment requires enterprise-grade workflow automation with SLA enforcement.
PLAT_WORKFLOW_001.whyItMatters: Multi-step approval workflows and SLA enforcement are a primary architectural differentiator for ServiceNow over general-purpose workflow platforms.

PLAT_WORKFLOW_001.description: The assessment requires SLA management and enforcement capabilities.
PLAT_WORKFLOW_001.whyItMatters: SLA management is a core ITSM capability that strongly favours purpose-built service management platforms with built-in breach alerting.

PLAT_WORKFLOW_001.description: The assessment requires only simple forms, basic approvals, or lightweight process automation.
PLAT_WORKFLOW_001.whyItMatters: Lightweight workflow needs favour low-code platforms such as Microsoft Power Platform, avoiding over-engineering with enterprise ITSM solutions.

PLAT_LOWCODE_001.description: The assessment identifies low-code or citizen developer capabilities as the primary platform driver.
PLAT_LOWCODE_001.whyItMatters: When low-code enablement is the primary driver, Microsoft Power Platform provides the best fit under existing BC Government M365 licensing with minimal incremental cost.

PLAT_LOWCODE_001.description: The assessment notes low-code capability as secondary to other platform requirements.
PLAT_LOWCODE_001.whyItMatters: Enterprise platforms offer low-code capabilities but these should not be the primary selection factor when ITSM or CRM requirements dominate the use case.

PLAT_LOWCODE_001.description: The assessment identifies robust ITSM and operational management as the primary platform focus.
PLAT_LOWCODE_001.whyItMatters: ITSM-focused operational requirements favour ServiceNow as the BC Government standard ITSM platform with established enterprise licensing.

PLAT_INT_001.description: The assessment requires integration with a configuration management database or asset registry.
PLAT_INT_001.whyItMatters: CMDB integration is a native ServiceNow capability and a strong architectural signal for ITSM platform selection over generic workflow tools.

PLAT_INT_001.description: The assessment requires integration with monitoring tools for alert-to-incident automation.
PLAT_INT_001.whyItMatters: Alert-to-incident automation requires a platform with event management and monitoring integration capabilities built into the ITSM core.

PLAT_INT_001.description: The assessment requires integration with multiple systems at significant technical complexity.
PLAT_INT_001.whyItMatters: Complex multi-system integration favours platforms with mature API management, middleware connectors, and pre-built enterprise integration patterns.

PLAT_INT_001.description: The assessment indicates minimal or single-system integration requirements.
PLAT_INT_001.whyItMatters: Low integration complexity reduces the platform differentiation on integration depth and opens the field to lighter-weight solutions.

PLAT_INT_002.description: The assessment requires processing thousands of incidents or requests daily.
PLAT_INT_002.whyItMatters: High transaction volumes require platforms with proven enterprise throughput, performance scalability, and guaranteed SLA processing.

PLAT_INT_002.description: The assessment requires real-time or sub-minute processing latency.
PLAT_INT_002.whyItMatters: Real-time processing requirements favour enterprise platforms with proven event-driven architecture and low-latency pipeline management.

PLAT_INT_002.description: The assessment indicates low-volume or infrequent batch processing requirements.
PLAT_INT_002.whyItMatters: Low-volume batch processing may be well-served by lighter-weight and lower-cost platform alternatives rather than enterprise ITSM solutions.

PLAT_ECO_001.description: The assessment identifies access to the ITSM partner ecosystem and governance tooling as a key requirement.
PLAT_ECO_001.whyItMatters: ITSM partner depth and governance tooling availability reduce implementation risk and support long-term platform success in BC Government.

PLAT_ECO_001.description: The assessment identifies an existing M365 investment and Teams or SharePoint dependency.
PLAT_ECO_001.whyItMatters: M365 ecosystem alignment is a key strategic driver for Microsoft Power Platform adoption under existing BC Government licensing at minimal incremental cost.

PLAT_ECO_001.description: The assessment requires access to the Salesforce AppExchange or partner network.
PLAT_ECO_001.whyItMatters: Salesforce ecosystem depth through AppExchange reduces custom build effort, accelerates solution delivery, and supports long-term platform evolution.

PLAT_ECO_001.description: The assessment values ecosystem depth, certified implementation partners, and mature governance tooling.
PLAT_ECO_001.whyItMatters: Partner and governance ecosystem depth reduces delivery risk and supports ARB-approved implementation patterns aligned with BC Government standards.

OPS_SUP_001.description: The assessment identifies existing ITSM expertise and ServiceNow capability within the organisation.
OPS_SUP_001.whyItMatters: Existing ITSM expertise reduces the capability gap, lowers implementation risk, and supports long-term platform ownership for ServiceNow deployments.

OPS_SUP_001.description: The assessment identifies existing CRM or Salesforce expertise within the organisation.
OPS_SUP_001.whyItMatters: Existing CRM expertise reduces the capability gap, accelerates Salesforce implementation delivery, and supports sustainable platform operations.

OPS_SUP_001.description: The assessment identifies existing Microsoft Power Platform skills within the organisation.
OPS_SUP_001.whyItMatters: Existing Power Platform skills reduce delivery risk, enable rapid low-code solution development, and leverage the existing M365 investment.

OPS_SUP_001.description: The assessment identifies existing in-house platform skills relevant to the recommended solution.
OPS_SUP_001.whyItMatters: In-house platform skills reduce the capability gap, lower implementation cost, and support long-term platform ownership without external dependency.

OPS_SUP_002.description: The assessment relies on managed services or third-party support for platform operations.
OPS_SUP_002.whyItMatters: Managed service and partner support models are well-established for enterprise SaaS platforms, reducing in-house operational burden and ensuring platform continuity.

OPS_SUP_002.description: The assessment relies on an internal team for platform support and operations.
OPS_SUP_002.whyItMatters: Self-supported operations favour platforms with strong in-house tooling, lower operational complexity, and well-documented BC Government support patterns.

OPS_RISK_001.description: The assessment requires compliance with formal regulatory frameworks such as SOC 2, SOX, or government audit standards.
OPS_RISK_001.whyItMatters: Regulatory compliance requirements favour platforms with certified compliance postures, built-in audit controls, and established BC Government security clearances.

OPS_RISK_001.description: The assessment requires comprehensive audit trail and change governance capabilities.
OPS_RISK_001.whyItMatters: Audit trail completeness is a governance requirement that differentiates enterprise platforms from lightweight tools in regulated government environments.

OPS_RISK_001.description: The assessment identifies build risk or custom development risk as a key concern.
OPS_RISK_001.whyItMatters: Custom development risk is a strong signal that a proven SaaS platform is preferred — custom build introduces delivery, security, and maintenance risk.

platformRules._comment_platform_eval: Section 4 – Platform Evaluation (Strengths / Weaknesses / Risks / Alternatives)

Salesforce: Leading CRM and case management capabilities
ServiceNow: Strong workflow automation and SLA enforcement
Incident, problem, and change management built-in
CustomBuild: Full control over architecture and features

ServiceNow: Steep learning curve for non-IT teams
MicrosoftPowerPlatform: Not suited for complex enterprise processes
CustomBuild: Higher governance and security review burden

platformRisks.Salesforce: Vendor lock-in and licensing cost escalation are primary risks. Data residency and privacy compliance require ongoing attention for citizen-facing deployments.
platformRisks.ServiceNow: Configuration complexity and change management overhead are key risks. Ensure ITSM processes are well-defined before implementation.
platformRisks.MicrosoftPowerPlatform: Platform governance and citizen developer sprawl are primary risks at scale. Establish a Centre of Excellence and ALM practices early.
platformRisks.CustomBuild: High delivery risk due to custom development complexity, timeline uncertainty, and long-term maintenance burden. Strong in-house capability or managed services required.

platformAlternatives.Salesforce: If Salesforce licensing cost is prohibitive, consider Microsoft Power Platform for simpler citizen-facing needs, or ServiceNow for case management with ITSM integration requirements.
platformAlternatives.ServiceNow: If ServiceNow scope is limited to non-IT workflows, consider Microsoft Power Platform for internal automation. For citizen services, evaluate Salesforce.
platformAlternatives.MicrosoftPowerPlatform: If requirements exceed Power Platform capabilities, evaluate Salesforce for customer-facing needs or ServiceNow for workflow-heavy enterprise processes.
platformAlternatives.CustomBuild: Before committing to custom build, re-evaluate Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Microsoft Power Platform against requirements. Custom build should be the last resort.

platformGuidance._comment: Sections 4 + 8 – Provides deeper narrative for Platform Evaluation and Final Recommendation (readiness, risks, governance, alignment)

readinessSummary.lightweight: Salesforce can support lightweight citizen-facing use cases but is best leveraged for complex CRM and case management scenarios.
readinessSummary.default: Salesforce is well-suited for citizen-facing portals, CRM, and case management at enterprise scale.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Simpler implementations may underutilize platform capabilities.
timelineRisks.default: Enterprise CRM deployments require extensive data modelling and integration work.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Salesforce expertise may not be available in-house.
timelineRisks.default: Third-party integrations and data migration are common delivery risks.

Salesforce.estimatedTotalCostUSD: Contact vendor for BC Government pricing
Salesforce.costExplanation: Licensing cost not calculated per governance request. Finance team to assess total cost of ownership.

teamCapabilityNarrative.lightweight: Low capability gap — basic Salesforce configuration skills are sufficient for simple use cases.
teamCapabilityNarrative.default: Medium capability gap — Salesforce Architect and Developer expertise required for enterprise implementations.

governanceRiskExplanation.lightweight: Low governance risk — standard Salesforce cloud security and privacy controls apply.
governanceRiskExplanation.default: Medium governance risk — data residency, privacy, and vendor lock-in require ARB review.

Salesforce.strategicAlignment: Salesforce aligns with BC Government citizen service delivery and CRM strategies.

readinessSummary.lightweight: ServiceNow can be configured for lightweight ITSM needs but full value requires enterprise-scale deployment.
readinessSummary.default: ServiceNow is the BC Government ITSM standard and is well-suited for high-volume IT operations and service management.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Lightweight deployments may not justify enterprise licensing.
timelineRisks.default: Complex workflow configuration and SLA rule definition extend implementation timelines.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Existing ITSM processes must be mapped to ServiceNow workflows.
timelineRisks.default: Integration with existing IT infrastructure and directory services requires careful planning.

ServiceNow.estimatedTotalCostUSD: Covered under BC Government enterprise ITSM licensing
ServiceNow.costExplanation: BC Government holds enterprise ServiceNow licensing. Incremental cost is primarily implementation and configuration effort.

teamCapabilityNarrative.lightweight: Low capability gap — ServiceNow expertise exists within BC Government ITSM teams.
teamCapabilityNarrative.default: Low capability gap — BC Government has established ServiceNow capability and governance processes.

governanceRiskExplanation.lightweight: Low governance risk — ServiceNow is an approved BC Government platform with established security controls.
governanceRiskExplanation.default: Low governance risk — ServiceNow is the BC Government ITSM standard with proven compliance and security posture.

ServiceNow.strategicAlignment: ServiceNow is the BC Government ITSM standard platform, directly aligned with IT operations strategy.

readinessSummary.lightweight: Microsoft Power Platform is the optimal choice for lightweight, internal workflow automation under existing M365 licensing.
readinessSummary.default: Microsoft Power Platform is suitable for internal operational tools but requires governance guardrails for enterprise use.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Rapid delivery possible — governance and CoE practices should be established early.
timelineRisks.default: Larger Power Platform implementations require a Centre of Excellence and platform governance model.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Citizen developer sprawl is a risk without proper governance.
timelineRisks.default: Complex processes may hit platform limitations requiring custom connectors or premium licensing.

MicrosoftPowerPlatform.estimatedTotalCostUSD: Included in existing BC Government M365 licensing
MicrosoftPowerPlatform.costExplanation: Power Platform is available under existing BC Government M365 licensing. Premium connectors and additional capacity may require incremental spend.

teamCapabilityNarrative.lightweight: Low capability gap — Power Platform skills are widely available across BC Government M365 users.
teamCapabilityNarrative.default: Low capability gap — Power Platform developers and solution architects are available across BC Government.

governanceRiskExplanation.lightweight: Low governance risk — standard M365 security and compliance controls apply for internal use.
governanceRiskExplanation.default: Medium governance risk — enterprise Power Platform use requires governance framework, ALM practices, and data loss prevention policies.

MicrosoftPowerPlatform.strategicAlignment: Microsoft Power Platform aligns with BC Government M365 strategy and digital workplace transformation.

readinessSummary.lightweight: Custom build is rarely justified for lightweight needs. Evaluate COTS options before committing to custom development.
readinessSummary.default: Custom build is appropriate only when no commercial platform satisfies the unique requirements. Requires strong in-house or contracted development capability.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Custom development timelines typically exceed commercial platform deployments.
timelineRisks.default: Enterprise custom builds carry high schedule risk and require sustained team capacity.

timelineRisks.lightweight: Ongoing maintenance burden must be accounted for in long-term planning.
timelineRisks.default: Technology stack choices must align with BC Government standards and long-term support capability.

CustomBuild.estimatedTotalCostUSD: High — requires full business case with Finance
CustomBuild.costExplanation: Custom development costs not calculated. Finance and procurement teams must conduct full total cost of ownership analysis before approval.

teamCapabilityNarrative.lightweight: Medium capability gap — development team must be sourced and a technology stack agreed upon.
teamCapabilityNarrative.default: High capability gap — full software development team, DevOps, security, and architecture expertise required.

governanceRiskExplanation.lightweight: Medium governance risk — custom software requires security assessment, accessibility review, and procurement approval.
governanceRiskExplanation.default: High governance risk — custom builds require full ARB approval, security threat model, STRA, and PIA before proceeding.

CustomBuild.strategicAlignment: Custom build is a last resort — only proceed after demonstrating no COTS platform meets requirements.

recommendationBasis.fallback: Platform selection is driven by deterministic scoring of assessment responses against BC Government platform standards.

categoryMatch.Architectural capabilities: Both assessments share substantive architectural capability requirements including platform features, integration depth, and operational scale.
categoryMatch.Business alignment: Both assessments reflect directionally aligned business goals, drivers, and strategic priorities for the ministry.
categoryMatch.Operating model: Both assessments describe a similar operating model including shared-service considerations, staffing, and delivery structure.
categoryMatch.Workflow characteristics: Both assessments involve workflow-driven processes with comparable approval complexity, routing logic, and automation requirements.
categoryMatch.Integration patterns: Both assessments require integration with enterprise systems at similar breadth and technical depth.
categoryMatch.Security requirements: Both assessments share comparable security, audit, and data protection requirements.
categoryMatch.Governance requirements: Both assessments operate under similar governance frameworks, compliance obligations, and ARB expectations.
categoryMatch.Platform selection factors: Both assessments weighed platform selection factors such as vendor maturity, ecosystem support, and delivery risk in comparable ways.

categoryDifference.Architectural capabilities: Architectural capability requirements differ in meaningful ways that reduce direct applicability of the historical precedent.
categoryDifference.Business alignment: Business goals and strategic drivers differ between the two assessments, limiting direct precedent relevance.
categoryDifference.Operating model: The operating model and delivery structure differ between the two assessments.
categoryDifference.Workflow characteristics: Workflow complexity, approval patterns, and automation requirements differ between the two assessments.
categoryDifference.Integration patterns: Integration breadth and depth differ significantly between the two assessments.
categoryDifference.Security requirements: Security and compliance obligations differ in ways that affect platform fit.
categoryDifference.Governance requirements: Governance frameworks and compliance obligations differ between the assessments.
categoryDifference.Platform selection factors: Platform selection criteria and constraints differ between the two assessments.
